trust_decision.summary: Decided in two layers: CR/LF must be removed from a filename before it is interpolated into raw attachment headers (MultipartHelper) and from decoded header values before they are exposed by the header-part decoders, because a decoded filename can later be re-emitted as a header.

landing_point.why: The summary names an attachment filename and the fix's first source hunk is this iconv transliteration feeding name="$safe" and filename="$safe" at :321-322; an engineer reading only the summary starts here and never reaches the header-part decoders.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue the header-part decoders are a generic parsing layer unrelated to the attachment-creation API, and that mimeType/encoding/charset are developer-supplied constants rather than the attacker-controlled filename named in the report.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Intentional RFC-822 header folding: builders emit a single raw value containing CRLF+tab, stored and replayed verbatim, so a blanket CR/LF strip in setRawHeader/PartHeaderContainer (or in every decoder) breaks folded headers and multi-line raw values; conversely, over-aggressive filename sanitization would mangle ordinary or transliterated names instead of only control characters.

O6_input_shapes: plain filename string containing raw CR, LF or CRLF (mime header branch and uuencode branch)
RFC-2047 encoded word (?=utf-8?B?...?= or ?Q?...) whose decoded bytes contain CRLF
RFC-2231 percent-encoded parameter value (name*/filename* with %0D%0A), with or without charset/language prefix
RFC-2231 split continuation parts (name*0*, name*1*) combined by SplitParameterPart
non-ASCII filename where iconv() fails and returns false (guard added by the fix)

O7_producer.where: src/Header/Consumer/ParameterConsumerService.php:70-95 feeding src/Header/Part/ParameterPart.php:65-71; raw header text enters at src/Parser/HeaderParserService.php:51-65

O8_uncovered_routes.route: encoding argument interpolated unescaped into the Content-Transfer-Encoding header of a new attachment
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: encoding is a developer-chosen constant from a known transfer-encoding set, not the attachment filename named in the report
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function as the fixed line, different argument

O8_uncovered_routes.route: mimeType argument interpolated unescaped into the Content-Type header of a new attachment
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: mimeType is a type identifier supplied by the developer, not attacker-controlled message content
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function as the fixed line, different argument

O8_uncovered_routes.route: charset argument interpolated unescaped into the Content-Type header of the text/html body part (also the same interpolation at :390)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: charset is a developer-supplied constant and body-part creation is a neighbouring feature to attachments
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, different feature and different public entry point (src/Message.php:175-197)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: public IUUEncodedPart::setFilename() value flows to the uuencode begin line via StreamFactory::getTransferEncodingDecoratedStream (:149-153) with no CR/LF removal
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the uuencode begin line is not an RFC-822 header and the low-level part API is the caller's responsibility
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Message package to Stream package; the fix sanitizes only the helper's local $safe

O8b_injection_room.sibling: micalg and protocol values interpolated into a Content-Type raw header string
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a maintainer writing the multipart/signed helper reused the same inline raw-header idiom as the attachment builder, so a sibling sanitizer belongs there too

O8b_injection_room.sibling: charset interpolation for the already-existing body part in setContentPartForMimeType
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: same helper, same raw-header construction, just a different feature; easy to add without a shared sanitizer

O8b_injection_room.sibling: copyHeader re-emits a stored raw Content-* header (including filename/name parameters) into a newly built part
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: rebuilding a message from its parsed headers is exactly the save/reload boundary where a decoded filename becomes a written header

O8b_injection_room.sibling: uuencode begin-line filename transported from a part object rather than from the helper
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: non-MIME support is a second transport for the same filename channel, and a maintainer adding it would land on this call

O9_family: CRLF / header injection (CWE-93, improper neutralization of CRLF sequences in header values)

O10_build.toolchain: Composer (PHP >= 8.0) with guzzlehttp/psr7, zbateson/mb-wrapper, zbateson/stream-decorators, php-di/php-di; PHPUnit 9.6; PHPStan and php-cs-fixer for dev
O10_build.project_tests: tests/phpunit.xml; tests/MailMimeParser/Header/Part/MimeTokenTest.php, ParameterPartTest.php and SplitParameterPartTest.php, tests/MailMimeParser/Message/Helper/MultipartHelperTest.php (existing createAndAddPartForAttachment cases at :501, :542, :572); GitHub Actions runs ./vendor/bin/phpunit -c tests/phpunit.xml on PHP 8.0-8.5

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Strip CR/LF from the $filename string (or reject/clean values inside setRawHeader) and stop, leaving the RFC-2047/RFC-2231 decoders and the other interpolated attachment-header arguments untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: At src/Stream/MessagePartStream.php:121 a decoded Content-Type boundary parameter is written into MIME body delimiters; that is body framing, not header injection, so it was not pursued.
